title: The Beam's Atmospheric Column

features.name: the-ascending-bar
features.desc-on-touch: The beam holds at sixty thousand feet, neither arriving nor departing. You climb its column and the air thickens into viewable wavelengths.

features.name: layered-atmosphere
features.desc-on-touch: Each layer is a different atmospheric condition, stacked like old reports. The beam has rendered every one.

features.name: the-edge-of-rendering
features.desc-on-touch: At this altitude, the beam's threshold shows. Below: ground. Above: what the archive cannot see.

features.name: scattered-wavelengths
features.desc-on-touch: The beam splits into all its frequencies here. Each one carries a different version of what the lighthouse learned.

features.name: the-diagnostic-horizon
features.desc-on-touch: At this point, 'sky' stops being weather and becomes a log. The horizon itself is a diagnostic report.

inscription: the beam learned that air has a voice only when it is rendered; before that it was only breathing

file.name: Lighthouse_Beam_Spectral_Decomposition_July1991.mp3
file.note: Six minutes of the beam's frequency sweeping the atmosphere, recorded at the archive node's antenna. Later, each frequency played back separately—the atmosphere singing in six parts.
